purpose: PET4D is a Slicer extension for dynamic, gated and static PET. It adds a DICOM plugin that loads PT series as sequences with SUV or Bq/ml values. It also provides modules for frame review and editing, motion correction, PET-to-CT/MR registration, and kinetic modelling (1TC, 2TC, Patlak, Logan, SRTM, SUVR). It is aimed at nuclear medicine researchers.
summary: I read the CMake files, the modeling module, the settings module and several helper libraries in full, and I searched all of the source. I found no network access, subprocess calls, pip installs, eval/exec, pickle, or text aimed at reviewers. The only deletion is a `shutil.rmtree` of the extension's own temporary export folder. The extension makes no environment changes beyond inserting its own module directory on sys.path. It uses only Slicer-bundled numpy, scipy, SimpleITK, pydicom and BRAINSFit. The LICENSE is MIT. The catalog entry is valid and uses `scm_revision` "main", a moving branch. CMake lists all the Python files the modules import. Minor points: large committed PNGs, the moving branch, and the absence of a clinical-use disclaimer. I did not read every file in full.
